meta.title: FARM127 Charlotte-Area Young Adult Resource Navigator
meta.description: A researched working directory of reputable resources in Charlotte, surrounding communities within roughly 30 miles, and essential statewide or national fallback programs.
meta.radiusDefinition: Local results are grouped by service location within roughly 30 road miles of Uptown Charlotte. This is a practical service-area screen, not a precise geospatial guarantee.

triage.backup: Use Safe Alliance, trafficking or crisis resources after immediate safety is addressed.
triage.limit: Do not use a routine referral process for an active emergency.

triage.situation: Suicidal thoughts or acute mental-health crisis
triage.limit: Call 911 when there is immediate danger or a medical emergency.

triage.situation: Homeless tonight or unsafe place to sleep
triage.backup: Ages 16–24: The Relatives On Ramp; men: Roof Above; women/children: Center of Hope.

triage.backup: Ask about VPA, GEAR Up, Medicaid and foster-specific education funds.
triage.limit: Many benefits end at 21; act quickly.

triage.backup: Use NC 211 and Mecklenburg Community Resource Centers for additional benefits.
triage.limit: Call before traveling; hours and capacity change.

triage.backup: Call 911 for immediate danger; Legal Aid/Charlotte Legal Advocacy for civil legal help.
triage.limit: Protect confidential location and contact information.

triage.situation: No food or basic household items
triage.firstAction: Apply for SNAP and contact Nourish Up
triage.backup: Crisis Assistance Free Store; Second Harvest food locator.

triage.situation: LGBTQ+ young adult needs affirming housing/support

triage.limit: Program age ranges and housing openings vary.

resources.name: NC 211
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult has multiple needs and FARM127 is unsure where to start.
resources.eligibility: Anyone in North Carolina.
resources.provides: Free, confidential, multilingual navigation to food, housing, health, transportation, legal and other community resources.
resources.access: Call 2-1-1, call 888-892-1162, or search the online database.
resources.caveat: Directory information changes; confirm the referred provider's current intake requirements.
resources.radiusNote: Located in or serving the requested roughly 30-mile Charlotte search area.

resources.supportAreas: Navigation / case management; Financial capability; Community / belonging
resources.name: Mecklenburg County Community Resource Centers
resources.referralTrigger: Help applying for county benefits or connecting to multiple county services.
resources.eligibility: Mecklenburg County residents; program-specific eligibility applies.
resources.provides: In-person access to benefit applications, case navigation and partner services.
resources.access: Visit a Community Resource Center or use Mecklenburg County's contact options.
resources.location: Ella B. Scarborough CRC, 430 Stitt Rd; Valerie C. Woodard CRC, 3205 Freedom Dr.
resources.caveat: Services and walk-in hours vary by site.
resources.radiusNote: Located in or serving the requested roughly 30-mile Charlotte search area.

resources.access: Search the online directory, then verify eligibility directly with the provider.
resources.caveat: A directory is a starting point, not a guarantee of availability.
resources.radiusNote: Located in or serving the requested roughly 30-mile Charlotte search area.

resources.supportAreas: Navigation / case management; Housing / homelessness; Community / belonging
resources.name: Mecklenburg Coordinated Entry
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult is homeless, sleeping somewhere unsafe, or likely to lose housing soon.
resources.eligibility: Individuals and families who are homeless or at risk in Mecklenburg County.
resources.provides: Community entry process for shelter, diversion, rapid rehousing and supportive housing resources.
resources.access: Call and complete a telephone assessment; follow instructions for an in-person assessment when requested.
resources.caveat: Housing is not immediate or guaranteed; callbacks may take up to two business days and programs have limited capacity.
resources.radiusNote: Located in or serving the requested roughly 30-mile Charlotte search area.

resources.supportAreas: Navigation / case management; Health care; Mental health / recovery
resources.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
resources.referralTrigger: Suicidal thoughts, mental-health crisis, severe emotional distress or concern about another person.
resources.eligibility: Anyone in the United States.
resources.provides: 24/7 call, text and chat crisis support and connection to local crisis services.
resources.access: Call or text 988. Call 911 for an immediate life-threatening emergency.
resources.location: Nationwide; routes to local crisis support.
resources.caveat: Not a replacement for emergency medical response when there is immediate danger.
resources.radiusNote: Statewide or national fallback resource accessible from the Charlotte area.

resources.provides: 24/7 crisis assessment, de-escalation and connection to treatment.
resources.access: Call the local mobile crisis line and select option 1.
resources.caveat: Response depends on safety, staffing and clinical assessment; call 911 for immediate danger.

resources.name: Mecklenburg County LINKS
resources.referralTrigger: A current or former foster youth needs independent-living planning, funding or case coordination.
resources.eligibility: Generally youth ages 13–21 who are or were in foster care; specific services depend on custody/status.
resources.provides: Independent-living assessment, planning, education, housing and other transition assistance.
resources.access: Contact Mecklenburg Youth and Family Services / LINKS.
resources.caveat: Age and custody rules are strict; refer before age 21 whenever possible.
resources.radiusNote: Located in or serving the requested roughly 30-mile Charlotte search area.

resources.supportAreas: Foster care; Soft skills / life skills; Transportation; Community / belonging
resources.name: Mecklenburg Phoenix Project
resources.referralTrigger: A former foster youth under 21 who is no longer in county custody needs transition support.
resources.eligibility: Young adults generally under age 21 who left foster care; confirm individual eligibility.
resources.provides: Post-custody independent-living support, case coordination and access to eligible funds/services.
resources.access: Call the Phoenix Project office and request an eligibility review.
resources.caveat: Do not wait until close to the 21st birthday; funding and services are eligibility-dependent.
resources.radiusNote: Located in or serving the requested roughly 30-mile Charlotte search area.

resources.supportAreas: Foster care; Financial capability; Community / belonging
resources.name: NC Foster Care 18 to 21 / Voluntary Placement Agreement
resources.referralTrigger: A youth is approaching age 18 in foster care and needs continued placement, case management or financial support.
resources.eligibility: Youth who meet North Carolina's criteria and enter a voluntary agreement; generally available until age 21.
resources.provides: Continued foster-care placement, case management, resources and financial assistance while pursuing an approved path.
resources.access: Ask the county social worker before discharge from care; review the state eligibility rules.
resources.location: North Carolina; administered through county child welfare.
resources.caveat: Timing matters. Leaving care without completing the agreement can make access harder.
resources.radiusNote: Statewide or national fallback resource accessible from the Charlotte area.

resources.name: Mecklenburg GEAR Up Supplemental Income Pilot
resources.referralTrigger: An eligible young adult aging out needs flexible monthly cash support for rent, food, transportation or other stability needs.
resources.eligibility: Pilot announced for certain Mecklenburg young adults ages 18–21 aging out of foster care.
resources.provides: Monthly supplemental income plus support coordination.
resources.access: Call Mecklenburg LINKS at 704-336-KIDS and ask whether the pilot is still enrolling or accepting referrals.
resources.caveat: Pilot status, enrollment slots and funding beyond the announced cohort were not confirmed for August 2026.
resources.radiusNote: Located in or serving the requested roughly 30-mile Charlotte search area.

resources.supportAreas: Foster care; Health care; Education; Community / belonging
resources.name: NC Medicaid for Former Foster Care Youth
resources.referralTrigger: A young adult who aged out of foster care needs health coverage.
resources.eligibility: Certain young adults under age 26 who were in foster care and enrolled in Medicaid when they aged out; rules depend on foster-care state and history.
resources.provides: Medicaid medical and behavioral-health coverage.
resources.access: Apply through ePASS or Mecklenburg County and explicitly identify former foster-care status.
resources.caveat: Eligibility details changed under federal/state policy; obtain a formal Medicaid determination rather than assuming eligibility.

resources.supportAreas: Foster care; Housing / homelessness; Health care; Financial capability; Community / belonging
resources.name: NC Medicaid Children and Families Specialty Plan
resources.referralTrigger: A Medicaid-enrolled young adult with current or former child-welfare involvement needs coordinated physical, behavioral and social care.
resources.eligibility: Eligible Medicaid beneficiaries involved with the child-welfare system, including certain former foster youth under 26.
resources.provides: Specialized Medicaid health plan with care management and trauma-informed provider coordination.

resources.caveat: Enrollment is eligibility-based; not every former foster youth will be automatically assigned.

resources.supportAreas: Foster care; Health care; Education; Community / belonging
resources.name: NC Reach
resources.referralTrigger: Paying tuition and school costs at a North Carolina public college or university.
resources.eligibility: Eligible NC residents who aged out of foster care at 18 or were adopted from foster care after age 12; must attend at least half time at an eligible NC public institution.
resources.provides: State-funded last-dollar scholarship and student support.
resources.access: Complete FAFSA and apply through NC Reach / CFNC.
resources.location: North Carolina public community colleges and universities.
resources.caveat: Deadlines and satisfactory academic progress apply; begin before enrollment.
resources.radiusNote: Statewide or national fallback resource accessible from the Charlotte area.

resources.supportAreas: Foster care; Housing / homelessness; Education; Financial capability; Community / belonging
resources.name: Education and Training Voucher (ETV)
resources.referralTrigger: Paying education, training, housing, books or other approved postsecondary costs.
resources.eligibility: Eligible current/former foster youth and some youth adopted or placed in guardianship; age and status rules apply.
resources.provides: Federal voucher funding of up to the program limit for eligible postsecondary expenses.
resources.access: Apply through the Foster Care to Success ETV portal and coordinate with LINKS/financial aid.
resources.caveat: Awards depend on eligibility, annual funding, enrollment and documentation; do not assume the full maximum.
resources.radiusNote: Statewide or national fallback resource accessible from the Charlotte area.
